name: Applio
description: Applio (IAHispano/Applio) — a polished RVC (Retrieval-based Voice Conversion) fork focused on ease of use and performance. Gradio WebUI entry point app.py launches on default port 6969; converts and clones voices from short training data and, in client mode, mounts a FastAPI app at /api. Tabs cover inference, training, TTS, model download, and audio analysis. Built on the RVC pipeline (RMVPE/crepe pitch extraction, .pth timbre models + .index feature retrieval). Gradio provides no authentication unless auth= is set, which Applio does not by default.
auth_notes: app.py's launch_gradio() calls Gradio launch() without auth=, so the WebUI on port 6969 is unauthenticated when server_name is 0.0.0.0. Applio also supports a --share flag that publishes a public *.gradio.live tunnel, and a client mode that mounts a FastAPI server at /api (additional unauthenticated REST surface). Any visitor can run inference, upload training audio, launch training, and use the built-in model-download tab to pull remote models. No login, token, or session in the default configuration.

shodan_dorks.rationale: Applio's non-default Gradio port 6969 is itself a strong narrowing signal; combined with the Gradio marker it is already fairly specific
Project name / branding rendered in the Gradio header; disambiguates Applio from upstream RVC and OpenVoice
Applio branding on its signature port 6969 plus the Inference tab label; near-unique to an Applio WebUI
Applio's model-download tab plus RVC index-rate parameter labels; identifies Applio even when moved off port 6969
Applio 3.x version marker in the header for version-targeted enumeration; adjust the version token per campaign

known_vulns: Gradio WebUI launched without auth= — unauthenticated inference, training-audio upload, and training-job control on port 6969
Client mode mounts a FastAPI app at /api with no auth key — additional unauthenticated REST surface (and /api/docs schema disclosure)
--share mode publishes a public *.gradio.live tunnel bypassing host/cloud firewalls
Built-in model-download tab fetches remote model URLs server-side — SSRF-style fetch and supply-chain (malicious model) risk
Gradio CVE-2023-51449 — /file path traversal (Gradio <4.11.0) leaks arbitrary host files and /proc/self/environ
Gradio CVE-2024-1561 — arbitrary local file read via /component_server (Gradio 4.3-4.12)
Gradio SSRF CVE-2024-4325 / CVE-2024-47167 — /queue/join save_url_to_cache fetches attacker-controlled URLs (internal-network / cloud-metadata pivot)
No rate limiting — GPU compute exhaustion via automated inference/training at operator cost
Uploaded audio and trained .pth/.index voice models are readable/downloadable through the UI file components with no access control
risk_notes: Applio is RVC with the friction removed — an approachable UI for cloning a voice from short training data — so an open 6969 instance lowers the bar for abuse further than raw RVC. (1) Non-consensual voice cloning / biometric-identity theft — any visitor uploads a target's audio, trains a .pth model, and generates converted speech in that voice; the built-in TTS tab adds text-to-cloned-voice directly. (2) Fraud / vishing / disinformation — the ease-of-use focus makes turnkey impersonation audio trivial to produce at operator GPU cost. (3) Model-download tab as SSRF / supply-chain vector — it fetches remote model URLs server-side, reachable for internal-network probing and for loading attacker-supplied models. (4) Training-data & model exposure — uploaded audio and trained .pth/.index models (downloadable through the file components and via Gradio file-read CVE-2023-51449 / CVE-2024-1561) are ready-made clone assets, and the CVEs also leak /proc/self/environ secrets. (5) FastAPI /api client mode adds an unauthenticated REST surface with its own /api/docs schema. (6) --share tunnels put the whole UI on the public internet under a throwaway gradio.live host. Applio shares the Gradio + RVC-parameter fingerprint with upstream RVC — disambiguate on the Applio branding and the model-download tab; port 6969 is itself a strong tell.
deployment_notes: Python or Docker on CUDA GPU hosts; a one-click Windows/macOS/Linux installer and Colab notebooks are the dominant paths, so many exposed instances are hobbyist and some use --share (public gradio.live URLs invisible to port scanners). Port 6969 is the Applio convention (distinct from upstream RVC's 7865 and Gradio's default 7860), which makes port 6969 + Gradio a useful narrowing filter — but the port is configurable via --port / DEFAULT_PORT, so confirm on branding. Client mode (--api) mounts a FastAPI server at /api. HuggingFace Spaces host Applio and Applio-derived demos, publicly indexed with no auth. Because Applio tracks the RVC pipeline, exposed instances are commonly on Gradio 4.x builds within the file-read/SSRF CVE range.
